extracted.intended_audience: teachers and general readers (and anyone redistributing Project Gutenberg eBooks)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and explanations governing which poems were chosen for a teachers' anthology (poems frequently requested by readers and suitable for classroom memorization), together with the Project Gutenberg redistribution/license requirements appended to the ebook.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection: poems most frequently requested
rubrics_metrics.description: Comprising the poems most frequently requested for publication in the magazine page 'Poems Our Readers Have Asked For'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection is explicitly demand-driven: the book collects poems that readers repeatedly asked to see printed in the magazine over a decade; when space or copyright prevented compliance the publishers sometimes could not fulfil requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suitability for school memorization
rubrics_metrics.description: Many of the selected poems 'are required or recommended for memorizing in state courses of study.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This feature makes the collection especially valuable to teachers throughout the country; inclusion favors poems used in state curricula or recommended for rote learning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial revision/proofreading
rubrics_metrics.description: Poems selected were 'carefully revising these for possible errors.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial standard: revise and correct earlier magazine printings before including them in the book to reduce transcription/printing errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion limited by original publication length
rubrics_metrics.description: Some poems are 'too long for insertion on our magazine Poetry Page' and thus included in the book instead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical constraint: magazine space limits may exclude long pieces; the anthology accommodates requested but longer works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright/permission requirement for copyrighted poems
rubrics_metrics.description: Special permission to use certain copyright poems has been granted through arrangement with the authorized publishers (explicitly acknowledged: Bobbs-Merrill, Charles Scribner's Sons, Harper and Brothers, Dodge Publishing, Lothrop Lee and Shepard, Little Brown, Houghton Mifflin, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inclusion of copyrighted material required obtaining permissions from rights-holders; the preface lists which publishers granted permission and which poems are covered.
